How is the ag labor shortage affecting agriculture in California? And is it limiting productivity or perhaps the diversity of crops at once we're raised in your state?

Ag labor has been an issue for decades for us. Obviously, it's something that is important. With a district like mine in the Central Valley, we grow 300 to 400 different types of commodities. A lot of specialty crops and a lot of them are very labor intensive from pruning to harvesting to everything else that is required around those types of products that are raised. So it's always a problem. Are we finding ways to bring in more automation? Yes. I mean, obviously if you take blueberries, for example, which has grown in many states, They used to be where people were very focused on picking specific blueberries that are ripe. Now they just take into account there's going to be a loss and they're harvesting mechanically and it's not as precise. And then they'll worry about getting the berries that aren't ready for market out at the processing plant. But yes, there was a point in time where even citrus Instead of going to the top of every tree, they were focused on the easier to reach quicker fruit in the middle of the tree and move on to the next tree because they didn't have enough labor to go after all the commodities. So you're actually losing a percentage of the crop there. So yeah, labor's been something that's impacted us for a long time.
